rv.q: The next stop on its leisurely jaunt around the world is a few months in Las Vegas, which surely says a lot about the general level of performance. Some tricks are less spectacular than others.

It's one of several adroit set pieces in a show that proves there's life yet in the ancient arts of wriggling out of a straitjacket and squeezing oneself into a dynamited safe – even if I found myself wishing pestilence on the four horsemen's overblown style.

Aside from the title and visual branding, however, the connection is fairly loose. A handful of early routines reference heists, while the Horsemen promise to steal our attention rather than our wallets, but any narrative ambitions are quickly abandoned in favour of a succession of increasingly ambitious illusions, ranging from intimate card tri...

Which makes what unfolded at the London Coliseum this week all the more remarkable. For two hours, a house full of hardened modern sceptics gasped, flinched and applauded like children. That, in itself, is a kind of magic.
